title: Fault matrix across two private runtimes with shared and dedicated holders: orphan replay, planned restart, crash checkpoint gaps, reboot metadata, update rollback, dirty worktrees, plugin failure and retention floors settle as typed outcomes

cases.summary: The peer runtime is added over the real argv transport and each runtime runs a parent. Real holders on real sockets: on each runtime a shared and a dedicated holder each run a program whose final bytes (`LAST-shared`, `LAST-dedicated`) arrive before its exit, with the bytes before exit equal to the holder's final offset (17 and 20). A recovery with another boot identity reports restored_metadata and adopts nothing while the program keeps running. server.restart on each runtime (the second through remote dispatch) hands the held program to a new control boot: preserved incarnations equal the live set, nothing ended or interrupted, the receipt is committed. A child on the peer is linked to the local parent; the peer is SIGSTOPped, the parent exits, and delivering the orphan notice stops at its deadline with the notice still owed (ack lost). Replacing the peer process re-proves the same machine (line epoch 2) and replays the notice: applied once, nothing left, and re-acknowledging it is a duplicate. The peer's parent incarnation is lost on the new runtime, the local parent is the one that exited (incarnation 1, no kills), and a relaunch on the peer starts incarnation 1 there.

A machine named disconnected mirrored remote sequence 41 and lost its line: the injected input.send to disconnected/t1 is machine_unreachable with last_seen_seq "41", ghost/t1 is not_found, and nothing runs locally. Update rollback across both runtimes: release 3.0.0 staged on the peer fails readiness and rolls back there (active stays 1.0.0, receipt failed with activation_failed, readable through remote dispatch and absent locally) while the local runtime's updates stay empty. Crash with a checkpoint gap on each runtime: the core is lost after checkpointing at MARK while a 4 KiB holder tail keeps less than the rest, so the survivor's screen is not exact and reports one gap ending at 8312. Losing the dedicated holder makes only its terminal unknown (holder_unreachable) while the shared one survives; no program is relaunched. A dirty worktree on each runtime is refused as checkout_dirty naming the checkout and kept. The peer is then crashed with an input.send in flight: outcome_unknown with its op_id, the roster keeps both machines unreachable, and a later call is machine_unreachable with no local fallback. A failing plugin is a durable failed run (exit 3), a missing program is action_unavailable, and a plugin printing 10 000 bytes keeps its 4 KiB tail with a visible output floor of 5904.
